title: LADDER: Diagnosing Domain-Level Self-Assessment Under Noisy Feedback
abstract: arXiv:2610.34737v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Knowing when they are reliable is essential for language models to support human-AI collaboration. Yet interaction feedback is not always complete or correct, and may mislead models' understanding of their own capabilities. We introduce LADDER to study how language models assess themselves under unreliable feedback. Our findings show that models can accurately report supplied performance information while still struggling to form trustworthy self-assessments from interaction experience. Apparently accurate assessments can obscure capability differences and do not necessarily predict future task performance. These findings suggest that trustworthy self-assessment should be evaluated against observed task performance and its predictive value. Our study provides empirical evidence of the limits of model self-knowledge and a basis for evaluating capability awareness in reliable human-AI collaboration.

translated_title: LADDER：诊断噪声反馈下的领域级自我评估
translated_abstract: 了解自身何时可靠，对于语言模型支持人机协作至关重要。然而交互反馈并不总是完整或正确的，可能会误导模型对自身能力的理解。我们提出LADDER来研究语言模型在不可靠反馈下如何进行自我评估。我们的发现表明，模型能够准确报告所提供的性能信息，但仍难以从交互经验中形成可信的自我评估。表面上准确的评估可能会掩盖能力差异，并不一定能预测未来的任务表现。这些发现表明，可信的自我评估应当基于观察到的任务表现及其预测价值来衡量。我们的研究为模型自我认知的局限性提供了实证证据，并为在可靠的人机协作中评估能力意识奠定了基础。
tldr: 提出LADDER框架研究语言模型在噪声反馈下的自我评估，发现模型虽能准确报告给定的性能信息，却难以从交互经验中形成可信的自我评估，表面准确的评估可能掩盖能力差异且无法预测未来任务表现。
en_tdlr: LADDER reveals that language models can accurately report supplied performance information yet struggle to form trustworthy self-assessments from noisy feedback, with seemingly accurate assessments masking capability differences and failing to predict future task performance.
